info.title: OperationsPizza API
info.summary: Employee scheduling, synchronised with TCP Humanity.
info.description:
The operations backend. Owns **scheduling**, and is the third Laravel service in
the NATS mesh alongside `pizzasys` (auth) and `HiringPizza` (employees).

## Who owns what

- **pizzasys** is the auth source of truth. Every bearer token here is verified
  against it on every request; nothing authenticates locally.
- **HiringPizza** is the employee source of truth *and the only writer of staff
  into Humanity*. When scheduling meets an employee with no Humanity link, this
  service asks over NATS and waits — two writers to one external system is how
  duplicate people get created.
- **TCP Humanity** is the source of truth for **shifts**. Every write goes there
  first, and a row exists here only because that write succeeded. A failed write
  therefore means nothing changed anywhere.

## Eight things that will bite you

Each one is a bug that looks like it works.

1. **`day_index` is computed server-side.** Never derive it client-side. The
   business week starts **Tuesday**, and that is a per-store setting
   (`week.week_start_dow`), not a constant.
2. **Use `duration_minutes`, never wall-clock arithmetic over start/end.** It is
   wrong on the two DST days a year: `22:00-06:00` is **9 hours** on the
   November fall-back night. That is the payroll number.
3. **A Shift's `id` is an *assignment* id, not a shift id.** One Humanity shift
   can hold several employees; the grid draws one card per person. Use the
   separate `shift_id` field to update or delete.
4. **Updates are `POST`, not `PUT`/`PATCH`** — house convention across these
   services.
5. **`EMPLOYEE_NOT_SYNCED` (409) is resumable, not a failure.** Nothing was
   written. Hold the user's input, poll `poll_url`, and replay.
6. **Bulk operations return `202` + a batch id and must be polled.** There is no
   rollback; failures come back per item with a retry endpoint.
7. **Publishing uploads `multipart/form-data` with a real `Blob`** —
   `canvas.toBlob()`, not `toDataURL()`.
8. **Shifts legitimately cross midnight.** The store closes at `00:00`, so
   `end_time <= start_time` is normal, not an error.

## Store scoping

Every route is store-scoped, and `{storeId}` is the **`store_number` string**
(e.g. `03759-00001`), matching HiringPizza — not the numeric primary key that
NATS events carry.

tags.name: Clocking
tags.description: Punches and live clock state, against TCP Manager+. Deliberately separate from the scheduling endpoints: shifts live in Humanity, worked time lives in TCP, and conflating them is what makes these integrations rot. Break punches (break-start / break-end) are NOT listed here: they are registered only when tcp.breaks_enabled is on, and it is off by default. A shift here is continuous expected work, so a break is not something the business schedules. The sync still handles a shift arriving as several segments regardless - anyone can punch out and back in at a physical clock.

get.description: Sits behind the same middleware as everything else, so a 200 here proves the pizzasys token verification, the service client and the auth rules are all wired correctly.

get.summary: Boot the whole grid in one call
get.description:
Returns roster, shifts, actuals, availability, time off, conflicts, stats and the published record for one week.

`week_start` may be **any day inside the week** — it is snapped to the store's configured week start (Tuesday for these stores), so clients never need to know the business-week rule.

parameters.name: week_start
parameters.description: Any date inside the target week. Defaults to today.

parameters.name: department
parameters.description: Filters the roster; shifts follow it, so a filtered grid never shows a card with no row to sit on.

get.description: For pickers that don't need a whole week. Active employees assigned to this store.
The Humanity positions mapped to this store. Only values that can actually match an employee.

post.description: **Writes to TCP Humanity first**, and only persists locally once that succeeded. So a failure means nothing changed anywhere — safe to retry, and safe to roll optimistic UI state back.

end_time.description: May be <= start_time; the store closes at 00:00, so crossing midnight is routine.

position_label.description: Position label, e.g. "Crew Member". Defaults to the employee's own label, then the store default.

force.description: Bypasses the conflict and availability guards after the manager confirms. Re-send the identical payload with this set.

parameters.name: shiftId
parameters.description: The `shift_id` field of a Shift, NOT its `id` (which is the assignment id).

post.description: House convention across these services. Changing `employee_id` reassigns the shift, which in Humanity is an unassign followed by an assign rather than a field edit.

delete.description: Removed from Humanity FIRST. If that fails nothing is deleted locally either — a shift invisible to managers but still live for the employee is the worst divergence available, so refetch rather than removing it from the UI.

parameters.name: confirm
parameters.description: Required for a published shift: employees may already have been notified by Humanity.

409.description: The shift is published and `confirm=true` was not supplied (`SHIFT_PUBLISHED`).

get.summary: Poll whether an employee is linked to Humanity yet
get.description: The other half of the `EMPLOYEE_NOT_SYNCED` flow. Poll roughly every 5s; when `synced` is true, replay the request that failed.

post.description:
For when the automatic request never landed. Publishes `operations.v1.employee.humanity_sync_requested` over NATS; **HiringPizza** does the actual write, because it is the only system allowed to create employees in Humanity. Repeated calls within 60s are de-duplicated.

Returns 200 (not 202) if the employee is already linked.

post.summary: Create or amend an actual shift
post.description: Local only — never pushed to Humanity. Passing `shift_assignment_id` amends the existing actual for that assignment rather than stacking a duplicate. `status` is derived, not accepted.

post.summary: Mark an actual shift as a no-show

day_of_week.description: Required when scope=weekly. CANONICAL 0=Sun..6=Sat — NOT the grid's Tuesday-based day_index. Convert at the API edge.

delete.description: Only overrides can be deleted. Profile-derived rules come from HiringPizza and must be changed there.

get.summary: Time off for a week, expanded per day

post.description: NOT pushed to Humanity: leave approval is a workflow that lives there, and pushing an unapproved entry would create a record nobody signed off on.

parameters.name: timeOffId
parameters.description: The `time_off_id` field, not the per-day synthetic `id`.

409.description: The entry came from Humanity (`TIME_OFF_READ_ONLY`) and would reappear on the next sync — withdraw it in Humanity instead.

post.summary: Snapshot a week into a reusable template
post.description: You don't send shifts — the given week is captured, stored week-relative by `day_index`.

get.summary: Read a template with its shifts

post.description:
Freezes the week's shift list and stores an optional screenshot as a FILE.

**multipart/form-data, and the screenshot must be a real Blob** — use `canvas.toBlob()`, not `toDataURL()`. An html2canvas render at scale 2 over a 10x7 grid is 1-3 MB, which has no business travelling as base64 in a JSON body.

Re-publishing the same week supersedes the previous record, so "the published week" is never ambiguous.

get.summary: Read a published week, with its frozen shift snapshot

delete.summary: Delete a published record and its screenshot

post.summary: Create a raw batch of shifts for one week in a single request
post.description: Queued, never synchronous, same as the other bulk endpoints. The one-hit alternative to looping POST /shifts per shift from the client. Unlike copy-week/apply-template, the shift list isn't derived from anything that already exists.

mode.description: `replace` wipes the target week first, sequencing the deletes before the creates.

position_label.description: Defaults to the employee's own position label if omitted.

post.description: Queued, never synchronous: a copy-week fans out into dozens of Humanity calls against an undocumented rate limit. Poll the returned batch id.

mode.description: `replace` wipes the target week first, sequencing the deletes before the creates.

post.summary: Apply a template to a week
Delete every shift in a week
post.description: Deletes real shifts in Humanity that employees may already be working from, so `confirm` is mandatory.

parameters.name: batchId
parameters.description: The ULID returned by a bulk endpoint.

get.description: Poll every ~2s while `queued` or `processing`, then refetch the week. `completed_with_errors` is a normal outcome — see the schema note on why there is no rollback.

post.description: Successful items are left alone and the failure counter is rolled back by the number retried, so progress stays truthful on the second pass. Returns 200 unchanged if nothing failed.

Writes a punch to TCP Manager+, which is the system of record for worked time. The open segment it produces is what makes the employee show as on the clock. Gated by EXTERNAL_WRITE_ALLOWED_STORES and TCP_WRITES_ENABLED.

at.description: Omit to punch now. Supplying a time makes this a CORRECTION, which is always verified against TCP rather than answered locally.

position_label.description: Resolves the TCP jobCodeId. Falls back to the store's default mapping.

409.description: Already clocked in, or the employee has no TCP link.
Not clocked in, or the employee has no TCP link.

get.summary: Whether this employee is on the clock
get.description: A local read, and correct for a punch made at a physical clock or in TCP's own app - the sync persists open segments, so this does not depend on the punch having come through this API.

linked_to_tcp.description: False means no tcp_employee_id has been replicated from hiring, so no hours can be attributed to them.

get.summary: Everyone on the clock at this store right now
get.description: One indexed query, no TCP call - so a dashboard may poll it. This was not previously possible: answering it meant a vendor request per employee, against an account-wide budget of 2500 a day.

post.summary: Fold other shifts' punches into this one
post.description: Two shifts were really one. The gap threshold that groups segments is a default, not a verdict, and only a person can overrule it; the result is pinned so the next sync leaves it alone. Sends nothing to TCP - grouping is our concept, and the hours are unchanged either way: the same punches, counted once.

post.summary: Move punches out of this shift into a new one
post.description: The mirror of merge: one shift was really two. Takes WorkSegment.id values (our row ids, not TCP's). Both the source and the new shift are pinned. At least one segment must be left behind.

422.description: The split would leave the source shift with no segments.

post.summary: Record a planned shift as a no-show
post.description: An absence is the ABSENCE of worked time: TCP models absence as leave rather than a segment, so this DELETES any segments behind the shift. Leaving them would keep paying someone who never turned up.

bearerAuth.description: A pizzasys Sanctum token. Verified upstream on every request, together with an authorization decision — so a valid token can still yield 403 on a route this subject may not use.

StoreId.name: storeId
StoreId.description: The store_number STRING (e.g. `03759-00001`), not the numeric primary key.

Error.description: Every domain failure uses this shape. Branch on `error.code`, never on the message.

message.description: Human-readable and safe to show to a user.
message.example: This employee already has an overlapping shift.

code.description: The machine-readable contract. See the `x-error-codes` section on the API root.

message.example: The shift date field is required.

allOf.description: Resumable. Nothing was written anywhere. HiringPizza has been asked over NATS to create the employee in Humanity; poll `poll_url` and replay the original request once `synced` is true.

id.description: The HiringPizza employee id, as a string.

role.description: The employee's position label, replicated as plain text.

color.description: Server-assigned and stable per employee, so a person is the same colour across sessions, devices and users.

is_active.description: Derived: true iff at least one store membership has an active status (hired/rehired).

synced.description: False means the employee has no TCP Humanity counterpart and CANNOT be scheduled yet.

hourly_rate.description: The employee's current hourly rate, or the store default when none is known. Not date-effective: this service keeps one current wage, not a pay history.

Shift.description: One card in the scheduling grid.

id.description: The shift ASSIGNMENT id, not the shift id. A Humanity shift can hold several employees and the grid draws one card per person.

shift_id.description: Use THIS for update and delete calls.

shift_date.description: Local business date of the shift's START.

day_index.description: Position within the requested week, computed server-side against the store's week_start_dow. Never derive this client-side.

starts_at.description: UTC instant. Use for sorting and overlap checks.

duration_minutes.description: True elapsed minutes in the store's timezone. USE THIS for hours — wall-clock arithmetic over start/end is wrong on the two DST days a year (22:00-06:00 is 540 minutes on the fall-back night, not 480), and this is the payroll-facing number.

crosses_midnight.description: Routine, not exceptional: the store closes at 00:00.

origin.description: `humanity`/`reconciler` means it was created or last changed in Humanity's own app, not here. Worth surfacing — it explains why an unfamiliar shift appeared, or why a local edit was overwritten. Humanity always wins.

ActualShift.description: A worked shift, as a manager reviews it - a ROLL-UP over one or more punched segments, not one row per punch. Punching out and back in closes a segment in TCP and opens another, so a single shift routinely arrives as several. Never pushed to Humanity; the hours behind it are written through to TCP.

planned_shift_id.description: The originating shift ASSIGNMENT id. Null for ad-hoc coverage.

end_time.description: NULL while the shift is still being worked. Branch on is_open rather than guessing from a missing value - filling in 'now' would make a running shift look finished.

duration_minutes.description: Minutes actually worked: the SUM of the segments, not the span between first in and last out. Time off the clock is not paid. On an open shift this is 'so far', and it stops accruing past tcp.rollup.max_shift_hours.

is_open.description: Somebody is on the clock and this shift has not finished.

time_variance.description: DERIVED server-side and never accepted from a client: how the worked shift compares to the plan behind it, on times and label. Recomputed freely by anything, including the background sync. Letting a caller assert it is how it drifts from the times it describes.

review_state.description: ASSERTED by a human, and the opposite of time_variance: only an explicit action sets it, nothing derives it, and no background job may overwrite it. That separation is what stops a sync turning a manager's no-show back into 'worked as planned'.

needs_attention.description: DERIVED. What the grid should put in front of a manager: a missed punch, a variance against the plan, hours that changed after they were signed off, or somebody who never clocked out. It exists so review_state can stay purely asserted - a clean shift raises nothing and needs no click.

grouping_pinned.description: ASSERTED. A manager has merged or split this shift's segments by hand, and the automatic grouper will not re-derive it. Safe to honour because grouping is ours: TCP has no concept of which segments form a shift, so it contradicts nothing TCP holds.

note.description: The MANAGER's note. Never overwritten by a sync - TCP's own segment notes live on each segment instead.

source.description: DERIVED from the segments' origin. Not derivable from merely HAVING segments, because a manager's hand-entry is pushed to TCP and gets one too.

segments.description: The punches behind this shift. Normally one - a shift is continuous expected work - but a manager needs to see all of them when somebody punched out and back in.

AvailabilityRule.description: A BLOCKED window. Hiring stores the inverse (when someone IS available); the backend inverts it against store hours and layers manager overrides on top. An employee with no availability on file is treated as fully available.

source.description: `employee_profile` is derived from their hiring record and is read-only here (change it in HiringPizza). `override` was entered by a manager and can be deleted.

TimeOffEntry.description: Already expanded to ONE ENTRY PER DAY, because the grid is per-day and shouldn't do calendar maths.

time_off_id.description: The underlying record; use this to delete.

origin.description: Humanity-sourced rows cannot be deleted here.

unpublished_at.description: Set when superseded by a later publish of the same week.

screenshot_url.description: A URL to a stored file, NOT a data URL.

shifts.description: The frozen snapshot. Only returned by the show endpoint.
Only returned by the show endpoint. Week-relative by design — that is what makes a template re-appliable to any week.

BulkOperation.description: There is deliberately NO ROLLBACK. Deleting shifts we already created in order to undo is more destructive than a partial week, especially once employees have seen it — so `completed_with_errors` is a normal outcome and failures are surfaced per item.

items.description: ONLY the failed items. A successful copy-week would otherwise return ~70 rows nobody reads.

sequence.description: In replace mode, deletes are sequenced before creates so a mid-run failure is visible rather than silently doubling the week.

synced.description: Poll until true, then replay the request that returned EMPLOYEE_NOT_SYNCED.

ScheduleWeek.description: Everything the grid needs in one round trip. Eight separate calls would show the user a week assembling itself piece by piece.

start.description: The TRUE week start, after snapping the requested date.

week_start_dow.description: 0=Sun..6=Sat. 2 (Tuesday) for these stores — a per-store setting, not a constant.

day_dates.description: Day-of-month numbers for the seven columns.

close_time.description: Midnight means the END of the day, never a zero-length day.

labor_cost.description: Real, from replicated pay history — the rate effective on each shift's date.

conflicts.description: Authoritative. Computed on UTC instants, so unlike a wall-clock client check it catches a 22:00-02:00 shift colliding with the next morning's 01:00-09:00 one.

Paginator.description: Standard Laravel length-aware paginator. Rows are in `data`.

WorkSegment.description: One punched segment, mirrored from TCP Manager+ exactly as TCP holds it. TCP owns every time on this object absolutely; nothing here is locally overridden. A segment with a null time_out is somebody on the clock RIGHT NOW - that is how live clock state is represented, rather than in a table of its own.

id.description: Our row id, which is what merge/split operate on.

time_in.description: Store-local wall clock, as TCP speaks it.

time_out.description: Null means OPEN: still on the clock.

duration_minutes.description: Null while open. The true UTC delta, so it stays correct across both DST transitions.

has_missed_punch.description: TCP flags a segment it knows is incomplete: the recorded time is a system default, not something the employee did.

origin.description: Where the punch was made. `punch` = our clock endpoints, `manual` = a manager hand-entered it, `discovered` = the sync found it already in TCP (a physical clock, or TCP's own UI). This is the one thing TCP cannot tell us afterwards, because it stores a segment identically however it was made.

note.description: TCP's own shiftNotes. Kept strictly apart from the manager's note on the shift.

Forbidden.description: pizzasys says this subject may not perform this action on this store. A permissions problem, not a bug.

NotFound.description: Store, shift or related record not found in this scope.

WriteConflict.description:
A guard rejected the write.

- `EMPLOYEE_NOT_SYNCED` — resumable; poll and replay (nothing was written).
- `SHIFT_CONFLICT`, `EMPLOYEE_UNAVAILABLE`, `EMPLOYEE_ON_TIME_OFF` — overridable; re-send the identical payload with `force: true` after the manager confirms.

UnprocessableWrite.description:
Either standard validation, or a domain error:

- `INVALID_LOCAL_TIME` — the wall-clock time does not exist (DST spring-forward).
- `STORE_NOT_MAPPED` / `POSITION_NOT_MAPPED` — a setup problem, not a user error: run `humanity:sync-catalog` and map the store.

HumanityWriteFailed.description: TCP Humanity rejected the write (`HUMANITY_WRITE_FAILED`). Nothing was persisted here — the write-through ordering guarantees it — so retrying is safe.

HumanityRateLimited.description: Humanity is throttling us (`HUMANITY_RATE_LIMITED`, its application status 91). Honour `Retry-After`.

BulkAccepted.description: Queued. Poll `GET /v1/stores/{storeId}/schedule/bulk/{batchId}` until status is terminal.

EMPLOYEE_NOT_SYNCED.action: Resumable. Poll the sync-status endpoint, then replay the original request.

SHIFT_PUBLISHED.action: Confirm with the user, then retry with ?confirm=true.

TIME_OFF_READ_ONLY.action: Explain it must be withdrawn in Humanity.

INVALID_LOCAL_TIME.action: The time does not exist (DST spring-forward). Ask for another.

STORE_NOT_MAPPED.action: Setup problem: the store has no Humanity location. Run humanity:sync-catalog.

POSITION_NOT_MAPPED.action: Setup problem: the store has no default Humanity position.

SHIFT_UNASSIGNED.action: The shift has no assignment to update. Should not happen; report it.

HUMANITY_WRITE_FAILED.action: Upstream rejected it. Nothing was saved; retrying is safe.
